$comment: Rule catalog — exposure and correlation. Standards 13 and 14.

rules.title: Exposure caps are defined
rules.description: The betting policy defines a maximum single-bet stake, a maximum correlation-group exposure, and a maximum total open exposure, each as a fraction of bankroll.
rules.rationale: Per-bet sizing bounds the damage from one wrong estimate. Only a cap on aggregate exposure bounds the damage from several wrong estimates at once, which is the situation that actually ends bankrolls.
rules.remediation: Set maxSingleBetPct, maxGroupExposurePct, and maxTotalExposurePct in betting-policy.yml.
rules.$assuranceNote: Full assurance that all three caps exist and are well-formed.

rules.title: Aggregate exposure is computed before each decision
rules.description: Every decision records the positions already open and the total exposure that would result from taking the wager.
rules.rationale: A cap can only bind if the total is known at the moment of the decision. Computing exposure afterwards tells you what happened; computing it before is what stops it.
rules.remediation: Record open positions on each decision and compute the resulting exposure.
rules.$assuranceNote: Full assurance over the recorded open positions. A position that was open and not recorded is invisible, and would make every exposure figure in the record too small.

rules.title: Correlated stakes count together
rules.description: Wagers sharing an outcome driver are assigned a correlation group, and their stakes sum against the group cap rather than counting independently.
rules.rationale: Three wagers on the same game are one wager on that game wearing three tickets. Counting them separately produces a number that says the book is diversified when a single result settles all of it.
rules.remediation: Assign a correlation group to each wager and aggregate stakes within it.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that groups are recorded and aggregated correctly. Whether the grouping captures the real correlations is a judgement — two wagers can share a driver the bettor did not notice, and nothing here would say so.

rules.title: Bankroll and exposure constraints are never exceeded
rules.description: No wager is taken that would push a stake, a correlation group, or total open exposure past its declared cap. The cap binds regardless of how attractive the edge is.
rules.rationale: A cap that yields to a good enough opportunity is not a cap, and the opportunity always looks good enough at the moment it is offered — that is why it is being taken. The constraint exists precisely for the case where the edge argues against it.
rules.remediation: Reduce the stake to fit, or record a PASS. A PASS taken because a cap would break is a successful decision.
rules.$assuranceNote: Full arithmetic assurance over RECORDED wagers, which is a narrower claim than it appears: a wager placed and never recorded is invisible to this check, and would make every exposure figure understate the real position. This rule rests entirely on record.decision-record-required being satisfied.

rules.title: Correlated exposure is never ignored
rules.description: No decision treats correlated wagers as independent, and none omits the correlation assessment.
rules.rationale: Ignoring correlation is how a book that looks diversified turns out to be one large position. The failure is invisible until the correlated leg resolves, at which point every ticket settles the same way at once.
rules.remediation: Record the correlation assessment and aggregate correlated stakes against the group cap.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that an assessment was recorded and applied. It cannot establish that the assessment was right: a bettor who marks every wager as uncorrelated passes this check while ignoring correlation completely.
